title: A. Kill Two Birds with One Stone

legend: You are given a binary matrix M$$$M$$$ of size n×m$$$n \times m$$$, where rows are numbered from 1$$$1$$$ to n$$$n$$$ from top to bottom and columns are numbered from 1$$$1$$$ to m$$$m$$$ from left to right. The position (r,c)$$$(r, c)$$$ denotes the cell in row r$$$r$$$ and column c$$$c$$$, where r$$$r$$$ and c$$$c$$$ are integers such that 1≤r≤n$$$1 \le r \le n$$$ and 1≤c≤m$$$1 \le c \le m$$$.

Initially, all entries of the matrix are 1$$$1$$$, except for exactly two cells which contain 0$$$0$$$. The two cells containing 0$$$0$$$ are located at positions (r1,c1)$$$(r_1, c_1)$$$ and (r2,c2)$$$(r_2, c_2)$$$.
You can apply the following two types of operations on the matrix:
1 r c – choose any position (r,c)$$$(r, c)$$$ with 1≤r<n$$$1 \le r  \lt  n$$$ and 1≤c≤m$$$1 \le c \le m$$$, and decrease both Mr,c$$$M_{r,c}$$$ and Mr+1,c$$$M_{r+1,c}$$$ by 1$$$1$$$.
2 r c – choose any position (r,c)$$$(r, c)$$$ with 1≤r≤n$$$1 \le r \le n$$$ and 1≤c<m$$$1 \le c  \lt  m$$$, and decrease both Mr,c$$$M_{r,c}$$$ and Mr,c+1$$$M_{r,c+1}$$$ by 1$$$1$$$.

In summary, in one move, you can select any two adjacent cells (sharing a side) in the matrix, and decrease both of the entries by 1$$$1$$$. You can apply the operations any number of times in any order. Your task is to determine whether it is possible to transform the matrix into a null matrix (i.e., a matrix where all entries are 0$$$0$$$).
input: The first line contains a single integer t$$$t$$$ (1≤t≤104$$$1 \le t \le 10^4$$$) — the number of test cases.

Each test case consists of a single line containing six space-separated integers n$$$n$$$, m$$$m$$$, r1$$$r_1$$$, c1$$$c_1$$$, r2$$$r_2$$$, c2$$$c_2$$$ (1≤n,m≤5⋅105; 1≤r1,r2≤n; 1≤c1,c2≤m; (r1,c1)≠(r2,c2); n⋅m>2$$$1 \le n, m \le 5 \cdot 10^5; \ 1 \le r_1, r_2 \le n; \ 1 \le c_1, c_2 \le m; \ (r_1, c_1) \ne (r_2, c_2); \ n \cdot m  \gt  2$$$) — the dimensions of the matrix and the positions of the two cells initially containing 0$$$0$$$.
It is guaranteed that the sum of n⋅m$$$n \cdot m$$$ over all test cases does not exceed 106$$$10^6$$$.
output: For each test case, output a single word in a line — YES if it is possible to transform the matrix into a null matrix, and NO otherwise.
